mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up this journey through “The Fact of a Body,” I hope you’re walking away with more than just a story. Maybe you’ve already noticed—searching for truth and justice? It’s rarely straightforward. The past, it doesn’t just stay behind us. The stories we inherit, and the ones we choose to tell, shape the way we see others... and even ourselves. So, what can you take with you from all this? Healing isn’t a finish line—it’s a process, and it unfolds one small step at a time. Justice? It’s not just about verdicts. It’s about the ongoing work of really understanding—yourself, and the world around you. Memory can feel heavy, or it can be a gift. Let it guide your choices, but don’t let it define who you are. Forgiveness isn’t a single moment—it’s something you choose, again and again, every day. And telling your story, even if it’s messy or unfinished? That’s an act of real courage and hope. As you move forward, just remember—everyone you meet is carrying their own hidden stories, old wounds, and unanswered questions. Healing—whether it’s personal or shared—takes time, patience, and the bravery to face discomfort. You don’t need to have it all figured out to get started. Sometimes, the bravest thing you can do is to keep asking questions, keep reaching out, and keep telling your truth, as best you can. In the end, it’s not about erasing pain or finding the perfect closure. It’s about learning to live with the messy, complicated parts of life, honoring what’s come before, and making space for hope. Your story matters. Your willingness to bear witness—to yourself, and to others—matters. So keep going. You’ve got this.
